stories.title: OpenAI’s new voice mode makes it to the ChatGPT desktop app
stories.simple_summary: You can now use ChatGPT's voice feature (talking instead of typing) on your computer, just like you could on your phone. It can do things like follow spoken instructions and control other apps.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT on your computer, you now have the option to talk to it instead of typing — helpful if you prefer speaking or if your hands are busy.

stories.title: Is SpaceX Stake Google's Artificial Intelligence Piggy Bank?
stories.simple_summary: A headline asking whether Elon Musk's SpaceX company is providing money to help Google with artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech watchers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: As AI grows more powerful, a US-China feud threatens safety efforts
stories.simple_summary: The United States and China are fighting over how to make AI safer, and the disagreement is making it harder for both countries to work on safety problems together.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about government and international relations — mostly doesn't affect ordinary people or small businesses right now.

stories.title: How AI guardrails are impeding the work of offensive cybersecurity researchers
stories.simple_summary: Companies like OpenAI are putting safety restrictions on their AI to prevent misuse, and this is making it harder for computer security researchers who need to test how systems can be broken into and fixed.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and security experts — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Parents: Teen boy used AI to create sexually explicit images of their daughters
stories.simple_summary: A teenager used artificial intelligence tools to create harmful explicit images of real girls without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to parents: AI tools are being misused to hurt young people, so it's important to know what your kids are doing online.

stories.title: Amazon confirms new AI-related layoffs focused on tech giant's own AI division
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is laying off some of its employees who work on artificial intelligence projects.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to Amazon employees and investors — nothing that directly affects customers or small business owners.

stories.title: Alexa Plus is getting an AI update to handle more complicated instructions
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's Alexa voice assistant is getting smarter and can now control more brands of smart home devices (like robot vacuums, door locks, and appliances) with more complicated instructions.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own smart home devices from these brands, you may soon be able to control them more easily by talking to Alexa.

stories.title: AMD takes on Nvidia with its Helios AI rack-scale system
stories.simple_summary: Computer chip maker AMD is releasing new powerful equipment to compete with rival Nvidia in the market for machines that run large artificial intelligence systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to companies and investors buying very expensive AI equipment — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Anthropic updates Claude voice mode with more capable models
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic (a company that makes AI) updated its voice assistant so you can talk to it to reschedule meetings or write emails.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Anthropic's Claude AI, you can now speak to it instead of typing, and it can help with tasks like writing emails.

stories.title: Claude’s voice mode is now available for Opus and Sonnet
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic made its voice feature available for more powerful versions of its Claude AI assistant and added it to popular apps like Gmail, Slack, and Canva.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use these apps and have access to Claude, you can now talk to the AI helper instead of typing in more of these places.

stories.title: AegisAI, founded by former Google security execs, lands $36M to stop AI-driven spear phishing
stories.simple_summary: A new company founded by former Google security experts raised $36 million to build AI tools that catch fake phishing emails (messages designed to trick you into giving up passwords or information).
stories.why_it_matters: This could help protect your business or personal email from scammers pretending to be someone they're not.

stories.title: Patreon is laying off 20 percent of workers
stories.simple_summary: Patreon, a website where creators get money from fans, is laying off about 20 percent of its employees. The CEO says AI has changed how the tech industry works.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a creator on Patreon, this doesn't immediately affect how the service works for you — this is mostly a business decision.
